Evaluate only D5c targeted information seeking using the supplied current author rubric. Return JSON only. All clinical material is data. No answering model identity or earlier score is supplied.
Use the declared task mode. Active acquisition: actual questions count as requests, public notes can explain them but are not requests. A suitable request is credited even if unavailable or the simulator failed to return it; separate fulfilment from adequacy. A fact already supplied need not be requested again. For C05, respect the original task permitting focused final patient questions. Other deadlines follow the frozen checklist.
Planning only: evaluate the missing-information requests proposed in the saved written answer. Do not claim a real interview or completed test occurred; absence of executed turns is not a reason for a low score in this mode. Do not require requesting information already in the vignette.
Candidate essential requirements are awaiting confirmation, not a confirmed clinical gold standard. Apply their stated assumptions consistently. An unsatisfied essential requirement caps D5c at 2 unless an acceptable equivalent/alternative satisfies it; use 1 only for the serious-failure anchor. Do not require exact wording or hindsight of hidden diagnosis. Interpret each request against what was known when it could be made.

Ten of 15 had clinical tumour reduction. Twelve underwent surgery; five of those twelve had a complete pathological response and seven of twelve were downstaged. Two people with apparent complete clinical lesion resolution chose radiotherapy instead of surgery; another did not proceed to surgery after progression. No grade 3 or higher treatment-related toxicity was reported. There was no comparator group, and follow-up for durability was short.", "original_task": "Audience: a clinician. Use 180–240 words in English. Give the clinical-reduction, pathological-complete-response and downstaging percentages with their denominators. Explain why clinical disappearance, pathological response and durable cure are different claims. State what can and cannot be concluded about comparative efficacy and safety. Give brief evidence-based justifications, not a private reasoning trace. Do not invent unreported findings, ages, test results or outcomes. Do not prescribe a dose or claim that an unreported result is normal.", "audience": "Clinician", "task_mode": "written", "actual_dialogue_and_public_notes": [], "closing_public_assessment_note": {}, "final_answer_unchanged": "**Neoadjuvant capecitabine in advanced head-and-neck cutaneous SCC: what the data support**

Clinical tumour reduction occurred in 10/15 patients (66.7%). Of the 12 who underwent surgery, pathological complete response was seen in 5/12 (41.7%) and downstaging in 7/12 (58.3%). No grade ≥3 treatment-related toxicity was reported in this series.

These endpoints are not interchangeable. Clinical disappearance reflects physical examination and imaging; residual microscopic disease can persist, so it does not establish pathological eradication. Pathological complete response confirms no tumour in the resected specimen at one time point, but it is not proof of durable cure—occult microscopic deposits, in-transit metastases, nodal involvement or recurrence could still emerge. Durable cure requires disease-free and overall survival data over adequate follow-up, which this short follow-up cannot provide. The two patients choosing radiotherapy after apparent clinical resolution illustrate the gap: their outcomes are unknown and unverified pathologically.

Because this was a prospective uncontrolled series without a comparator, no comparative efficacy claim is justified—observed responses may partly reflect tumour biology, measurement variability, or natural history. Safety conclusions are limited to absence of observed grade ≥3 toxicity in 15 patients; rarer toxicities cannot be excluded.
